records.name: Foster Grandparents (City of Philadelphia)
records.summary: Adults 55 and older with limited income who spend their days in pre-K and elementary classrooms, giving one-on-one help to children ages 3 to 7 and earning a stipend for their time.
records.what_you_do: Work in a classroom under a teacher's supervision, giving children one-on-one attention. Volunteers attend an information session, pass a background check, and go through orientation before starting.

schedule.text: 15 to 40 hours a week in a classroom, during the school year

locations.label: Program office (placements are at schools citywide)

cost.text: Free to join; volunteers receive a stipend (the page does not give the amount)

first_step.how: Fill out the online interest form, attend an information session (bring a state ID or license and proof of income), consent to a background check, then attend orientation
first_step.basis: Needs an application, an information session and a background check before you see the work

records.notes: City page has no dates, so status is based on a working official page. Stipend amount not published. Phone not listed on the page.

records.name: Senior Companion Program (Philadelphia Corporation for Aging)
records.summary: Volunteers aged 55 and up who visit older adults living at home who are lonely or have health or sight challenges, offering friendship and steady company.
records.what_you_do: Visit one older adult on a regular schedule, keep them company, and help them stay connected. Volunteers complete a background check and special training first.

schedule.text: Volunteers commit at least 20 hours a week

locations.label: PCA main office (visits happen where the older adult lives)

cost.text: Free to volunteer; volunteers receive a cash stipend and travel reimbursement

first_step.how: Contact the Philadelphia Corporation for Aging; the article does not describe the application steps
first_step.basis: Background checks and special training come before service, and the public article does not describe how to apply

records.notes: Program facts come from a WHYY profile last updated July 21, 2025, which reports about 43 active volunteers. The PCA site was not searched for this program page itself, so check the phone line before sending anyone.

records.name: Center in the Park
records.summary: A senior community center in Germantown for adults 55 and up, with fitness classes, pottery, a choir, trips, and staff who help with housing and benefits.
records.what_you_do: Take fitness, massage, pottery, arts, or choir sessions, join breakfast and lunch, go on day trips, or sign up for benefits and housing counseling.

schedule.text: Weekday activities; the center posts a calendar of classes and trips

cost.text: Free membership for adults 55 and older

first_step.how: Use the Become a Member page or call the center at 215-848-7722
first_step.basis: Membership is free and open to adults 55 and older, with a clear way to sign up; the site does not describe a drop-in policy

records.notes: Hours are not listed on the site. The site lists a full day of activities on October 7, 2026, and a December trip with no year given.

records.name: Northern Living Center
records.summary: A senior community center on North Franklin Street with group exercise, games, crafts, music, outings, and one-on-one help with Medicare, Social Security, and other benefits.
records.what_you_do: Join exercise and wellness sessions, play games or billiards, take part in arts and crafts or workshops, or book a benefits counseling appointment.

schedule.text: Monday to Friday, 7:30 am to 4 pm; Thursday until 7 pm; Saturdays by schedule only

first_step.how: Call the center, submit the online senior application, or visit to schedule a tour
first_step.basis: Older adults are welcome and there is a clear way to start: call, apply online, or come in for a tour

records.notes: Age minimum is not stated; the center says to call and confirm eligibility. The site has no dated events. It is partnered with North City Congress.

records.name: Peter Bressi Northeast Senior Center
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia senior center on Frankford Avenue with bingo, cards, exercise, computer lessons, trips, and a caseworker who helps with benefits.
records.what_you_do: Play cards or bingo, take an exercise class, learn computers, join a cooking event or trip, or talk with a caseworker about rent rebates, PACE, or housing.

schedule.text: Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm

first_step.how: Call (215) 831-2926 or stop by for a guided tour
first_step.basis: Invites visitors to tour the center; membership steps are not on the page

records.notes: Newest dated item on the site is a December 2023 notice; the rest are 2022 newsletters and flyers. Status is dormant on dated evidence, but the center may still run. Call before sending anyone. Riders 65 and older can use SEPTA shared ride, per the page.

records.name: Marconi Older Adult Program
records.summary: A program for adults 50 and older at the South Philadelphia Boys and Girls Club, with a grab-and-go lunch, coffee and conversation, games, crafts, technology classes, fitness, and trips.
records.what_you_do: Come for lunch and conversation, take a tech or art class, join a fitness session, get help with resources, or go on a trip. The program also offers rides and wellness phone calls.

schedule.text: Hours are not listed on the page; call to ask

locations.label: South Philadelphia Boys and Girls Club

first_step.how: Call the program through the Contact Us page or the club at (215) 218-0800
first_step.basis: The page gives a contact route but does not describe how to enroll

records.notes: Page shows only a 2024 copyright and no dated news. The page's contact line gives a different number from the South Philadelphia club number used above; verify by phone before listing.

records.name: Center at Journey's Way
records.summary: A community center for adults 55 and older in Roxborough, run by Intercommunity Action, with a café style lunch, fitness and art classes, and volunteer roles.
records.what_you_do: Eat lunch in the dining room, take a fitness class or an art or learning class, volunteer, or join social activities during open hours.

first_step.how: Visit any weekday during open hours; no appointment is mentioned
first_step.basis: Anyone 55 and older can walk in on a weekday; how membership works is not explained

records.notes: No phone number on the page, so the general Interact email is listed. The page has no dated news; the only date is the 2009 move to Rector Street. Fetched without the www prefix because the www host had a certificate mismatch.

records.name: Lutheran Settlement House Senior Center
records.summary: A senior center for adults 55 and older run by Lutheran Settlement House on Frankford Avenue. The website does not list specific programs or hours, so call to ask what is running.
records.what_you_do: The center describes itself as a place to grow, learn, and look after one another. Ask staff which classes or meals are running.

first_step.how: Call the general line at 215-426-8610 to ask how to enroll
first_step.basis: Enrollment and drop-in rules are not explained on the page

records.notes: Thin page: no programs, hours, email or dated news. Status is probably_active only because the official site is working. Lutheran Settlement House's senior services page (lutheransettlement.org/lsh-services/senior-services/) was named but not fetched.

records.name: PHA Senior Centers (Wilson Park, Cassie L. Holley, Emlen Arms)
records.summary: Free senior centers at three Philadelphia Housing Authority sites, open to housing residents and to seniors from the wider community. Members take part in meals, dance and exercise classes, movies, and trips around the city.
records.what_you_do: Eat a balanced meal, join a dance, walking or aerobic class, watch a movie, go on a trip, or get help with daily activities.

schedule.text: Activity times are not listed on the page

cost.text: Free; the Philadelphia Housing Authority and the Philadelphia Corporation for Aging pay for the services

first_step.how: Call Carla Fleming at 215-684-3959, the one contact the page lists for all three centers
first_step.basis: Open to seniors from the wider community as well as PHA residents, with a published phone contact

records.notes: Addresses are as the PHA page gives them. An older directory listed Wilson Park at 2508 Jackson St. and spelled the center Cassie L. Holly; check the spelling and street number when calling. No minimum age is stated.

notes: Interest family seniors-intergenerational, lane G. Nine records published, all checked on their own sites or a public government or news page. Budget: used 9 of 10 WebSearch calls and about 28 WebFetch calls. Dropped with reasons: (1) Caring for Friends (caringforfriends.org) is a food bank whose homebound meal program is listed, but the site does not confirm volunteer visits, and a separate lovable.app site describing visits was not verified; not published. (2) Ennoble Care hospice volunteer listings (ennoblecare.com) do not name Philadelphia on the site; the Philadelphia listing came from Idealist, a lead site; not published. (3) On Lok House (219 N. 10th St.) is affordable senior apartments, not a community group, and its waiting list is open; not published as a group. (4) Heartland Hospice and Surrey Services serve Delaware, Chester or Bucks counties, not Philadelphia; not in scope. (5) AccentCare Hospice and Dove Hospice Philadelphia listings are hospice volunteer postings from Idealist, a lead site, with no own-site check; not published. (6) Halcyon Hospice listing is in Philadelphia, Mississippi; out of area. Dated evidence is thin for many senior centers, which is why most are probably_active on working sites. Consider a future pass on the PCA senior center network (28 PCA-funded centers, daily lunch for 60 and older) using PCA's Find a Senior Center tool, which was not reachable from this search budget. The Little Brothers, KleinLife and Penn's Village leads are the best next fetches once their hosts respond.
